opts.t: Primary, scene, history, secondary, reassess, impression
opts.why: Order: scene size-up, primary, history (OPQRST and SAMPLE), secondary, field impression and interventions, reassessment.

opts.t: Scene, history, primary, secondary, impression, reassess
opts.why: Order: scene size-up, primary, history (OPQRST and SAMPLE), secondary, field impression and interventions, reassessment.

opts.t: Scene, primary, history, secondary, field impression and interventions, reassessment

opts.t: History, scene, secondary, primary, impression, reassess

q: You have not touched the patient yet. Which scene pack matches this recap?

opts.t: BSI, scene safety, MOI/NOI, number of patients, extra resources
opts.why: Scene before contact: BSI/PPE, safety for you/partner/patient/bystanders, MOI vs NOI, number of patients, extra resources.

opts.t: AVPU, OPQRST, SAMPLE, then BSI

q: When do you consider early law enforcement from this recap?

opts.t: Only after you finish a detailed head-to-toe
opts.why: Call law early if you suspect abuse/violence or the scene is unsafe or heating up.

opts.t: Abuse or violence suspected, or the scene feels unsafe or escalating
opts.why: Call law early if you suspect abuse/violence or the scene is unsafe or heating up.

opts.t: Every medical call so you have a witness
opts.why: Call law early if you suspect abuse/violence or the scene is unsafe or heating up.

opts.t: Only if the patient asks you to call police
opts.why: Call law early if you suspect abuse/violence or the scene is unsafe or heating up.

q: Alert and oriented ×4 versus confused / V / P / U — which consent pair?

opts.t: AOx4 is implied; V/P/U is expressed
opts.why: Alert and oriented ×4 → likely decision-making capacity → expressed consent. Confused / V / P / U → implied consent.

opts.t: Both are expressed if a family member is present
opts.why: Alert and oriented ×4 → likely decision-making capacity → expressed consent. Confused / V / P / U → implied consent.

opts.t: AOx4 is likely capacity and expressed consent; confused / V / P / U is implied consent
opts.why: Alert and oriented ×4 → likely decision-making capacity → expressed consent. Confused / V / P / U → implied consent.

opts.t: Consent waits until after the secondary exam
opts.why: Alert and oriented ×4 → likely decision-making capacity → expressed consent. Confused / V / P / U → implied consent.

q: Snoring, gurgling, and stridor without a stethoscope — what do they mean?

opts.t: Snoring is fluid, gurgling is tongue, stridor is wheeze in the chest
opts.why: Upper airway, no stethoscope: snoring = tongue; gurgling = fluid → suction; stridor = upper swelling/constriction.

opts.t: Snoring is tongue, gurgling is fluid so you suction, stridor is upper swelling
opts.why: Upper airway, no stethoscope: snoring = tongue; gurgling = fluid → suction; stridor = upper swelling/constriction.

opts.t: All three are lower-airway sounds you need a stethoscope for
opts.why: Upper airway, no stethoscope: snoring = tongue; gurgling = fluid → suction; stridor = upper swelling/constriction.

opts.t: Snoring is anaphylaxis, gurgling is asthma, stridor is pneumonia
opts.why: Upper airway, no stethoscope: snoring = tongue; gurgling = fluid → suction; stridor = upper swelling/constriction.

q: Adult breathing rate and the three lower-airway sounds from this recap?

opts.t: 8–12. Wheeze is fluid, crackles are mucus, rhonchi are bronchoconstriction
opts.why: Adult normal 12–20. Stethoscope on the chest: wheeze = bronchoconstriction; crackles = fluid in alveoli; rhonchi = mucus/congestion.

opts.t: 12–20. Wheeze is bronchoconstriction (often exhalation), crackles are alveolar fluid, rhonchi are mucus/congestion
opts.why: Adult normal 12–20. Stethoscope on the chest: wheeze = bronchoconstriction; crackles = fluid in alveoli; rhonchi = mucus/congestion.

opts.t: 20–30. All three are heard without a stethoscope at the mouth
opts.why: Adult normal 12–20. Stethoscope on the chest: wheeze = bronchoconstriction; crackles = fluid in alveoli; rhonchi = mucus/congestion.

opts.t: 12–20. Wheeze is tongue, crackles are stridor, rhonchi are gurgling
opts.why: Adult normal 12–20. Stethoscope on the chest: wheeze = bronchoconstriction; crackles = fluid in alveoli; rhonchi = mucus/congestion.

q: Adult pulse and what you do the moment you see major bleeding?

opts.t: 40–60. Finish SAMPLE first, then dress the bleed
opts.why: Adult pulse 60–100. Major bleeding is a life threat — stop and treat it when you see it.

opts.t: 100–140. Wait for the rapid scan
opts.why: Adult pulse 60–100. Major bleeding is a life threat — stop and treat it when you see it.

opts.t: 60–100. Stop and treat the life threat as soon as you see it
opts.why: Adult pulse 60–100. Major bleeding is a life threat — stop and treat it when you see it.

opts.t: 60–100. Document it and treat after the hospital handoff
opts.why: Adult pulse 60–100. Major bleeding is a life threat — stop and treat it when you see it.

q: Which pair is OPQRST versus SAMPLE from this recap?

opts.t: OPQRST is allergies and meds; SAMPLE is onset and severity
opts.why: OPQRST = present illness, especially pain or breathing. SAMPLE = broader history (signs, allergies, meds, past hx, last oral, events).

opts.t: OPQRST is present illness (pain/breathing); SAMPLE is the broader medical history
opts.why: OPQRST = present illness, especially pain or breathing. SAMPLE = broader history (signs, allergies, meds, past hx, last oral, events).

opts.t: Both are only for trauma
opts.why: OPQRST = present illness, especially pain or breathing. SAMPLE = broader history (signs, allergies, meds, past hx, last oral, events).

opts.t: SAMPLE replaces AVPU on medical calls
opts.why: OPQRST = present illness, especially pain or breathing. SAMPLE = broader history (signs, allergies, meds, past hx, last oral, events).

q: They deny alcohol. You still suspect it. What does this recap want?

opts.t: Keep asking until they confess or you refuse transport
opts.why: Ask calmly. You may re-ask once, then drop it and write that they deny use. Reasonable decisions with the facts you had.

opts.t: You may re-ask once, then drop it and document that the patient denies alcohol or drug use
opts.why: Ask calmly. You may re-ask once, then drop it and write that they deny use. Reasonable decisions with the facts you had.

opts.t: Write that they are intoxicated as a fact
opts.why: Ask calmly. You may re-ask once, then drop it and write that they deny use. Reasonable decisions with the facts you had.

opts.t: Skip documentation so you are not liable
opts.why: Ask calmly. You may re-ask once, then drop it and write that they deny use. Reasonable decisions with the facts you had.

q: Suspected abuse — report and chart from this recap?

opts.t: Wait for proof. Writing a suspicion is defamation
opts.why: Mandatory report on suspicion. Reporting suspicion is not defamation. Defamation is stating false guilt as fact. Write what you see and quoted speech.

opts.t: Mandatory report of the suspicion. Chart observations and quotes, not “that person IS an abuser”
opts.why: Mandatory report on suspicion. Reporting suspicion is not defamation. Defamation is stating false guilt as fact. Write what you see and quoted speech.

opts.t: Only report if the patient asks you to
opts.why: Mandatory report on suspicion. Reporting suspicion is not defamation. Defamation is stating false guilt as fact. Write what you see and quoted speech.

opts.t: Call medical control instead of authorities
opts.why: Mandatory report on suspicion. Reporting suspicion is not defamation. Defamation is stating false guilt as fact. Write what you see and quoted speech.

q: Childbearing-age female with lower abdominal pain. What do you ask?

opts.t: Nothing about pregnancy unless they volunteer it
opts.why: Treat them as possibly pregnant. Ask chance of pregnancy and last menstrual period. Document the answer they give.

opts.t: Any chance of pregnancy, and when was the last menstrual period
opts.why: Treat them as possibly pregnant. Ask chance of pregnancy and last menstrual period. Document the answer they give.

opts.t: Only STI history, never LMP
opts.why: Treat them as possibly pregnant. Ask chance of pregnancy and last menstrual period. Document the answer they give.

opts.t: Only if they are over 40
opts.why: Treat them as possibly pregnant. Ask chance of pregnancy and last menstrual period. Document the answer they give.

q: Focused exam versus detailed head-to-toe — who gets which?

opts.t: Focused for the unresponsive; detailed for every talking medical patient
opts.why: Focused = responsive medical who can point at the problem. Detailed = unresponsive, significant MOI (ejection, high speed, big fall), or suspected hidden/multiple injuries.

opts.t: Focused for a responsive medical patient who can localize; detailed for unresponsive, significant MOI, or hidden/multiple injuries
opts.why: Focused = responsive medical who can point at the problem. Detailed = unresponsive, significant MOI (ejection, high speed, big fall), or suspected hidden/multiple injuries.

opts.t: Always detailed so you never miss anything
opts.why: Focused = responsive medical who can point at the problem. Detailed = unresponsive, significant MOI (ejection, high speed, big fall), or suspected hidden/multiple injuries.

opts.t: Focused only after you give medications
opts.why: Focused = responsive medical who can point at the problem. Detailed = unresponsive, significant MOI (ejection, high speed, big fall), or suspected hidden/multiple injuries.

q: Adult systolic band and the pediatric minimum under age 10?

opts.t: 80–140 adult. Ped min is age × 10
opts.why: Adult systolic 90–120; <90 hypotension/shock; 120–130 hypertension range. Under 10: 2×age+70. Age 10 hits 90, then adult cutoff.

opts.t: 90–120 adult. Under 90 is hypotension. Ped min = 2 × age + 70. At 10 years you use the adult 90 cutoff
opts.why: Adult systolic 90–120; <90 hypotension/shock; 120–130 hypertension range. Under 10: 2×age+70. Age 10 hits 90, then adult cutoff.

opts.t: 100–160 adult. Ped min is always 90
opts.why: Adult systolic 90–120; <90 hypotension/shock; 120–130 hypertension range. Under 10: 2×age+70. Age 10 hits 90, then adult cutoff.

opts.t: 90–120 adult. Ped min = age + 90
opts.why: Adult systolic 90–120; <90 hypotension/shock; 120–130 hypertension range. Under 10: 2×age+70. Age 10 hits 90, then adult cutoff.

q: GCS ranges from this recap?

opts.t: Eyes 1–6, verbal 1–4, motor 1–5. Total 0–15
opts.why: E 1–4, V 1–5, M 1–6. Total 3–15. Memorize the table.

opts.t: Eyes 1–4, verbal 1–5, motor 1–6. Total 3–15. 15 is fully alert. 3 is no response
opts.why: E 1–4, V 1–5, M 1–6. Total 3–15. Memorize the table.

opts.t: One number 1–10 only
opts.why: E 1–4, V 1–5, M 1–6. Total 3–15. Memorize the table.

opts.t: Eyes 0–4, verbal 0–5, motor 0–6. Total 0–15
opts.why: E 1–4, V 1–5, M 1–6. Total 3–15. Memorize the table.

q: PERRL and the pinpoint versus dilated hint from this recap?

opts.t: PERRL is pulse equal. Pinpoint is stimulants. Dilated is opioids
opts.why: PERRL. Both constrict together. Note unequal, blown, sluggish. Pinpoint often opioids. Dilated often stimulants or brain injury.

opts.t: Pupils equal, round, reactive to light. Pinpoint often opioids/downers. Dilated often stimulants or brain injury
opts.why: PERRL. Both constrict together. Note unequal, blown, sluggish. Pinpoint often opioids. Dilated often stimulants or brain injury.

opts.t: Only the left pupil matters
opts.why: PERRL. Both constrict together. Note unequal, blown, sluggish. Pinpoint often opioids. Dilated often stimulants or brain injury.

opts.t: Fixed and dilated is a normal finding after oxygen
opts.why: PERRL. Both constrict together. Note unequal, blown, sluggish. Pinpoint often opioids. Dilated often stimulants or brain injury.

q: SpO2 target and the carbon monoxide trap?

opts.t: 80–85%. CO makes the number falsely low
opts.why: Desired 94–99%. CO can look falsely high. Saturation is percent occupied, not red-cell count.

opts.t: 100% only. CO is not mentioned
opts.why: Desired 94–99%. CO can look falsely high. Saturation is percent occupied, not red-cell count.

opts.t: 94–99%. CO can read falsely high because the machine treats CO as occupied hemoglobin. It does not count how many red cells you have
opts.why: Desired 94–99%. CO can look falsely high. Saturation is percent occupied, not red-cell count.

opts.t: 70–80%. You ignore the number if they are talking
opts.why: Desired 94–99%. CO can look falsely high. Saturation is percent occupied, not red-cell count.

q: Glucose numbers and when you check from this recap?

opts.t: 40–60 normal. Check only known trauma
opts.why: Normal 80–120 mg/dL. <80 hypoglycemia. Those three looks can mimic each other.

opts.t: 80–120. Under 80 is low. Check altered/unconscious, known diabetics, and stroke vs intoxication vs hypoglycemia
opts.why: Normal 80–120 mg/dL. <80 hypoglycemia. Those three looks can mimic each other.

opts.t: 150–200 normal. Never check if they look drunk
opts.why: Normal 80–120 mg/dL. <80 hypoglycemia. Those three looks can mimic each other.

opts.t: 80–120. Over 80 is always shock
opts.why: Normal 80–120 mg/dL. <80 hypoglycemia. Those three looks can mimic each other.

q: Breathing is inadequate. One option is assist ventilations. One is give a drug. What first?

opts.t: Give the drug. ABCs wait for medications
opts.why: Priority rule: ABCs and life threats BEFORE medications. Inadequate breathing → ventilate first.

opts.t: Ventilate first. ABCs and life threats before medications
opts.why: Priority rule: ABCs and life threats BEFORE medications. Inadequate breathing → ventilate first.

opts.t: Skip both and start SAMPLE
opts.why: Priority rule: ABCs and life threats BEFORE medications. Inadequate breathing → ventilate first.

opts.t: Call for a detailed head-to-toe first
opts.why: Priority rule: ABCs and life threats BEFORE medications. Inadequate breathing → ventilate first.

q: Reassessment clocks from this recap?

opts.t: Unstable about every 5 minutes. Stable about every 15. Recheck MS/GCS, ABCs, vitals, response to treatment
opts.why: Unstable/critical ~5 min. Stable ~15. Recheck mental status/GCS, ABCs, vitals, treatment response. Then a structured handoff.

opts.t: Everyone every 30 minutes
opts.why: Unstable/critical ~5 min. Stable ~15. Recheck mental status/GCS, ABCs, vitals, treatment response. Then a structured handoff.

opts.t: Unstable every 15. Stable every 5
opts.why: Unstable/critical ~5 min. Stable ~15. Recheck mental status/GCS, ABCs, vitals, treatment response. Then a structured handoff.

opts.t: Only once at the hospital door
opts.why: Unstable/critical ~5 min. Stable ~15. Recheck mental status/GCS, ABCs, vitals, treatment response. Then a structured handoff.
